clue.text: Feeling guilty, has made blunders

indicators.note: to blunder is to make a mess, so the letters of the two words beside it are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone feels guilty because they have made mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who feels guilty about what they did feels shame, which is this adjective's sense.

clue.text: Means it won't play a principal part

definitions.meaning: a means or instrument by which something is done

definitions.text: it won't play a principal part
definitions.meaning: a firm acting on behalf of a principal rather than for itself

explanation.definitionFit: It means both the means by which something happens and a business acting for others.

clue.text: Does it secure tile to shingle?

definitions.text: Does it secure tile to shingle?

parts.words: Does it secure tile to shingle?
parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat, and a shingle is a short women's haircut; a long pin fixes one to the other

explanation.surface: A roofer's question about fixing tiles to wooden shingles.
explanation.walkthrough: Roofing is the picture, but 'tile' is old slang for a hat and a 'shingle' is a 1920s short bob haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: This long pin pierces a hat and the hair beneath to hold it in place.

clue.text: Composer to drive men wild

indicators.note: wild suggests disorder, so the three words' letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A composer whose music drives men to frenzy.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian was a composer of early operas such as L'Orfeo.

clue.text: Desert watercourse

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to abandon something and a trench carrying water.

clue.text: Dish of caviare that one is greedy to have

definitions.text: that one is greedy to have

indicators.note: to dish something is to mess it up or spoil it, so the letters of the fish-roe word are scrambled

explanation.surface: A plate of caviar is something a greedy person would want.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a roundabout phrase: the quality a greedy person possesses. 'Dish of' looks like serving food but tells you to rearrange CAVIARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Greed and this noun are synonyms: it is the quality a greedy person has.

clue.text: Teach unit members to become trustworthy

indicators.note: to become something else means the letters are changed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Teaching the members of a unit to be reliable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'members' is a link: the letters of TEACH and UNIT, the members, become the answer when rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something genuine and reliable can be trusted, a near synonym.

clue.text: A long way off getting a rising service

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the RAF (Royal Air Force) is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: Someone far away joins an up-and-coming armed service.
explanation.definitionFit: Something at a great distance is this adverb, as in seen from far away.

clue.text: Like the fare if it's too high?

definitions.text: Like the fare if it's too high?

parts.words: Like the fare if it's too high?
parts.note: high meat has gone off, making the food (fare) uneatable

explanation.surface: Complaining about an overpriced bus or train ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' and 'high' suggest a costly ticket; it is food, and high game has gone off.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has gone off and is unfit to eat is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Modules which are used in teaching chemistry

definitions.text: which are used in teaching chemistry
definitions.meaning: the substances of the periodic table taught in chemistry

explanation.definitionFit: The word means basic components and also the chemical substances of the periodic table.

clue.text: Dispatched to the interior?

parts.note: food that has been dispatched (finished off) has gone inside the body, not off to inland regions

explanation.surface: Something has been sent off inland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dispatched' suggests being posted, and 'interior' a country's inland; the joke is food polished off and sent into the stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Food consumed has been swallowed and sent to the body's interior.

clue.text: Parisian summit conference

parts.note: a French phrase meaning head to head, a private talk between two people, like a summit between two leaders

explanation.surface: A summit meeting of world leaders held in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parisian' says the answer is French; literally 'head to head', with 'summit' playing on head as top.
explanation.definitionFit: This French phrase names a private conversation between two people, a meeting of two heads.

clue.text: In the sphere of misdeeds this is a record

definitions.text: In the sphere of misdeeds this is a record

parts.words: In the sphere of misdeeds this is a record
parts.note: a document listing offences committed, kept by police or the army

explanation.surface: A record-breaking feat in the world of wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' tempts as a best-ever achievement; it is a written record of offences.
explanation.definitionFit: This document is the written record of offences charged against a person.

clue.text: Headlong plunge into disreputable bar

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a head-first leap and, informally, a sleazy bar or club.

clue.text: Some grates may be designed as fuel-savers

indicators.note: the letters are designed afresh into a new shape

explanation.surface: Certain fire grates might be built to save fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fuel-savers' are storage tanks holding fuel, not economical devices.
explanation.definitionFit: These large tanks store town gas, so they keep fuel for later use.

clue.text: It enables one to cross without being observed

definitions.text: It enables one to cross without being observed

parts.words: It enables one to cross without being observed
parts.note: voters mark their cross on the paper in private, so no one sees how they voted

explanation.surface: Something that lets a person cross over unseen, like a smuggler's route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' suggests crossing a border; it is the X a voter marks on a ballot paper in private.
explanation.definitionFit: A vote cast in private, with the voter's choice marked unseen, is this voting system.

clue.text: Slow worker causing delay

parts.note: to retard is to slow down
an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: A sluggish employee holds things up.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance that slows a process, as fire retardant does, is causing delay.

clue.text: Simple or complicated requests

indicators.note: made complicated means jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Requests can be simple or complex.
explanation.definitionFit: To beg or plead is to request urgently, so this verb is a stronger synonym.

clue.text: Interval at recent play

indicators.note: to play with letters is to move them around

explanation.surface: An interval during a modern stage play.
explanation.definitionFit: This French term names the interval between acts of a play, or music played then.

clue.text: It may reveal hidden charges

parts.note: explosive charges buried underground are found by this device

explanation.surface: Something that exposes concealed fees on a bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hidden charges' reads as concealed fees; the charges are explosives buried in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: This device locates buried explosive devices, the hidden charges of the clue.

clue.text: How two auxiliary verbs act?

parts.note: be is an auxiliary verb in English
have is the other auxiliary verb

explanation.surface: A grammar question about how helping verbs work.
explanation.definitionFit: To act in a certain way, especially properly, is this verb, a synonym.

clue.text: The coming of the Christian faith

definitions.text: The coming of the Christian faith

parts.words: The coming of the Christian faith
parts.note: the season before Christmas marking the coming of Christ

explanation.surface: The arrival of Christianity in a land.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads as the spread of Christianity; it is the church season awaiting Christ's coming.
explanation.definitionFit: This word means an arrival and is the Christian season before Christmas.

clue.text: The French way to get fat

parts.note: la is a French word for 'the'
RD is the abbreviation of road, a way

explanation.surface: Asking how French cooking makes people put on weight.
explanation.definitionFit: This is rendered pig fat used in cooking, so it is a kind of fat.

clue.text: Game boss producing good position for expansion

parts.note: bridge is a card game
a head is the boss or chief

explanation.surface: A gaming chief creates a strong base from which to grow.
explanation.definitionFit: A military foothold in enemy territory from which an army can advance is this position.

clue.text: Waterways that could link Kirkcaldy to Keswick

indicators.note: linking the two towns joins the tail of the first place name
joined to the head of the next place name

explanation.surface: Canals that might connect a Scottish town with an English one.
explanation.walkthrough: The end of Kirkcaldy (DY) joins the start of Keswick (KES). Kirkcaldy is in Fife, Scotland; Keswick is in the Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: Dykes are ditches or channels for water, so they are waterways.

clue.text: Game is southern game

parts.note: tag is a children's chasing game

explanation.surface: Asking whether one sport is a southern one.
explanation.definitionFit: A male deer is hunted, so it is game in the hunting sense.

clue.text: A course people follow

parts.note: a race is a people or ethnic group
to track someone is to follow them

explanation.surface: A path that the crowd walks along.
explanation.definitionFit: A course for horses or cars to race on is this circuit.

clue.text: Girl admits publicity dodge

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the girl's name takes the publicity word inside it

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name
an ad is publicity

explanation.surface: A girl confesses to a publicity trick.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge something is to escape or avoid it, a synonym.

clue.text: This leg break shows quickness of the hand

indicators.note: to break the words up and reassemble them, a cricketer's leg-break hinting at the spin

explanation.surface: A leg-spinning ball shows a bowler's quick hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leg break' reads as a cricket delivery spinning from the leg side; 'break' is the anagram signal on THIS LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'sleight of hand' shows this noun means dexterity, deft quickness of the fingers.

clue.text: Dubious character?

definitions.meaning: a person, as in a suspicious character the police wish to question

explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective meaning doubtful and a noun for a person thought guilty.
